target.projectDescription: starlette 0.26.1 (starlette/__init__.py __version__) - the starlette ASGI framework/library source tree: request/response/routing/static-files/websocket framework for building ASGI apps. Server side: routing.Router.__call__ iterates routes; Route/WebSocketRoute.matches() regex-match scope['path'] and build path_params via match.groupdict() + convertor.convert; Mount.matches() pops the remainder 'path' param and rewrites child scope['path']/root_path; StaticFiles.__call__(scope) -> get_path(scope) = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(*scope['path'].split('/'))) -> get_response(path) -> anyio.to_thread.run_sync(self.lookup_path, path) where lookup_path joins directory+path, realpath/abspath canonicalizes, commonprefix containment-checks and os.stat()s, then FileResponse(full_path) whose __call__ re-stats (anyio.to_thread.run_sync(os.stat, self.path)) and serves via anyio.open_file(self.path, mode='rb') + file.read(chunk_size); requests.Request (url/headers/query_params/path_params/cookies accessors over scope, stream() body via self._receive(), _get_form multipart parsing via MultiPartParser into SpooledTemporaryFile wrapped by UploadFile(filename=Content-Disposition filename)); middleware/wsgi.py builds WSGI PATH_INFO from scope['path']; templating.Jinja2Templates (jinja2.FileSystemLoader(directory), env.get_template(name)); config.Config (open(env_file) read, os.environ via Environ wrapper).

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: The audit target is the starlette framework itself, so the untrusted-input boundaries are the ASGI scope (the dict the ASGI server hands to every __call__(scope, receive, send) entry point - it carries the request path, method, headers, query_string, and the routed path_params the router injects) and the receive() message stream (raw body chunks): (1) scope['path'] reads - StaticFiles.get_path at staticfiles.py:111 (os.path.normpath(os.path.join(*scope['path'].split('/'))) - THE dominant attacker-controlled file-location input, fed into lookup_path), staticfiles.py:141, Route.matches at routing.py:238, WebSocketRoute.matches at :316, Mount.matches at :388, Router.__call__ redirect_slashes at :732/:734/:735/:737, URL.__init__ at datastructures.py:34, WSGI PATH_INFO at middleware/wsgi.py:25; (2) routed path variables - match.groupdict() at routing.py:240/:318/:391 (regex match over scope['path'] producing path_params), matched_params.pop('path') at routing.py:394 (Mount remainder that becomes the child scope['path']), scope.get('path_params', {}) at routing.py:243/:321/:396/:481 and requests.py:124 (request.path_params accessor); (3) request headers - scope['headers'] reads at datastructures.py:38/:534 (URL host header, Headers.__init__), <x>.headers.get(...) call sites (requests.py:130 cookie, :257 Content-Type, :312 server-push; routing.py:475 host; middleware/gzip.py:20 Accept-Encoding, middleware/trustedhost.py:38 host, middleware/cors.py:80 origin / :107 access-control-request-headers, middleware/errors.py:247 accept, datastructures.py:452 upload content-type, testclient.py:233), StaticFiles Not-Modified subscripts request_headers['if-none-match']/['if-modified-since'] at staticfiles.py:227/:235, self.headers['Content-Type'] at formparsers.py:228; (4) multipart upload filenames - MultiPartParser.on_headers_finished reads options[b'name']/:b'filename'] from the Content-Disposition parse (formparsers.py:194/:206), the filename is stored on UploadFile(filename=...) at formparsers.py:209-214 while the CONTENT goes to an auto-named SpooledTemporaryFile (formparsers.py:207) - the upload filename never reaches a filesystem path in this tree; (6) raw wire - self._receive() calls at requests.py:221/:301 (Request body loop) and websockets.py:35/:45 (WebSocket.receive), websocket.receive() at endpoints.py:77, and the message.get('body')/:get('type')/:get('more_body') reads at requests.py:223/:226/:303 plus the websocket message.get reads at endpoints.py:83/:106/:120 (middleware/base.py message.get reads are response-direction and excluded); the stream/headers parameters of FormParser/MultiPartParser (formparsers.py:48-54/:122-127) and the receive parameter of Request.__init__ (requests.py:194); (7) ASGI entry parameters - the `scope` parameter of the ~44 ASGI callable functions across the package (every __call__/matches/handle/lifespan signature) is the framework-injected carrier of all HTTP input; The dominant filesystem-operation channels are: os.path.join (staticfiles.py:83/:111/:136/:166), os.path.normpath (:82/:111), os.path.abspath/realpath (:168/:170/:171), os.path.commonprefix containment check (:172), os.stat direct (:177) and via anyio.to_thread.run_sync (staticfiles.py:209, responses.py:335), os.path.isdir/isfile (staticfiles.py:56/:85, config.py:62), anyio.open_file (responses.py:353 - the serving read), builtin open (config.py:121), FileResponse construction (staticfiles.py:154/:192), file.read chunked transmission (responses.py:356), SpooledTemporaryFile (formparsers.py:207), UploadFile.file write/read/seek/close (formparsers.py:263/:266, datastructures.py:465-484), jinja2.FileSystemLoader/get_template (templating.py:85/:94/:112), importlib.util.find_spec (staticfiles.py:79).

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO source or sink row is expected to resolve at API level: the file-access channels flow through os.path/anyio/jinja2 members that are not part of the database (only the starlette tree is), and the input channels are ASGI scope dict reads, framework-injected objects and Content-Disposition option dicts that API graphs cannot bind to module members. The column is kept 'ast' for all families for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name/subscript text, syntactic receiver, scope/request/headers/options name conventions). os.path.join / os.stat / anyio.open_file / anyio.to_thread.run_sync / jinja2.FileSystemLoader are matched by their syntactic module-qualified shapes (os.path.* Attribute chains, anyio.* Attribute chains, jinja2.* Attribute chain) with moduleHint carrying the stdlib/external module path; member-name matching on instance members (file.read, part.file.write, self.file.write, headers.get, match.groupdict, matched_params.pop) is receiver-name-based on purpose; name-collision noise (a .read()/.get() on an unrelated object) is constrained by module/file and receiver-shape restrictions and left to labeling.

uncoveredCases: Async/await indirection: StaticFiles.get_response offloads the real file work via anyio.to_thread.run_sync(self.lookup_path, path) (staticfiles.py:121/:137/:150) and FileResponse.__call__ via anyio.open_file (responses.py:353); the run_sync wrapper rows capture the path argument (argument 1) but the taint step from the ASGI scope through get_path/get_response/lookup_path into these calls requires data-flow modeling in Phase 2 (MySummaries), not extraction rows.

Dynamic dispatch ambiguity: .headers.get/.get calls are name-based; a non-Headers receiver with a .get member inside the matched module set would produce a false candidate row (no such collision observed on the request path in this snapshot; receivers like request/self.headers/headers/request_headers are emitted as hints).

Chained assignment targets: scope['headers'] = list(scope['headers']) at datastructures.py:534 assigns through a subscript target inside a chained assignment; write targets are excluded via Assign.getATarget() (plural accessor) so the RHS read at :534 is captured while the target occurrence is not - if a future CodeQL version models chained targets differently, this row could double-count (verified against python-all 7.1.2).

Starred join argument: os.path.join(*scope['path'].split('/')) at staticfiles.py:111 passes the split components as a starred unpack; the row reports arg_index 0 (the positional slot the starred expression occupies) - the per-component flow is left to labeling/data-flow.
os.path.splitext/re.sub path munging in schemas.py (_remove_converter, schemas.py:86-93) operates on ROUTE definitions (operator strings), not request paths - not extracted; documented here.

mimetypes.guess_type at responses.py:36/:303 receives filename or path but performs no filesystem access (string matching against a type map) - deliberately not a sink row; if a future labeling round wants it as a propagation node it should be a summary, not a sink.

Test client scope construction (testclient.py:236-258) builds the scope dict literal including 'path': unquote(path) - the dict literal keys are not subscripts, so only the unquote calls are captured; the mapping from unquote result into scope['path'] for downstream consumers is a data-flow concern (MySummaries), recorded here.

Import-qualified name matching: anyio/jinja2 members are matched by syntactic Attribute chains (anyio.to_thread.run_sync, anyio.open_file, jinja2.FileSystemLoader); an aliased import (import anyio as x) would be missed - not observed in this snapshot (all modules use plain `import anyio` / `import jinja2` / `import os`).
